shared many of the burdens incident to the publication of the paper, and was a regular contributor to its columns, and one who always stood squarely by the paper. I shall never cease to miss him. He was a man that more than any other man aided the paper to gather its support than any other man I have known. He was loyal to his fellow-workers. Well do I remember the last conversation I had with him at the meeting of the Southern Baptist Convention in Houston. He grasped my hand in his he spoke words of encouragement. I have seen our dear friend since then—never—ever since. Until did I think then that never again would I see him.

The year of his formal connection with the College is somewhat uncertain, but it is known that Reverend Holland was on the Savoy College faculty from the fall of 1886 to the spring of 1889, when he was replaced by Haskell. He was a member of the church from the fall of 1886 to the spring of 1889. He was a member of the church. After this he became a Baptist, to which denomination he has devoted most of his life. He became a member of the church and became a Baptist, to which denomination he made many contributions, to which denomination the many years.

He was a friend to every good cause. Simple in his ways and frugal, he never turned from his duty. A man of intense convictions and firm in maintaining them. He had the courage of his convictions and found them to be unfailing. He was a stalwart Baptist, able to defend the cause of truth. He was a loyal contributor to university at large for many years until Jesus comes again.

He was connected with the State dis-convention for many years. He was a vice-president of the State Baptist convention. He was a vice-president of the State Baptist convention. And was a Vice-President of the Howard College, and was President of the Board of Florence University for many years.

Doctor and Miss Montgomery also served the interest of the Church and of higher education, and their services were without compensation, for love of Christ alone delivered to us. He never grew too old to learn, and remained a student all his life. A man of intense convictions and firm in maintaining them.

Doctor and Miss Montgomery were contributors of the church for many years. Yet such men as you and your co-laborers among us have made the ways to be longer, the fields larger than they are now.

He was connected with the State Baptist convention for many years. He was a vice-president of the State Baptist convention. And was a Vice-President of the Howard College, and was President of the Board of Florence University for many years to 1903 to 1938.
